What the hub lays over a session row whose record, or whose workspace's
record, is damaged on its machine ({@link DamagedRecordReport}): the file,
why, and the way out that removes it (`archive`: archive workspace
`workspaceId`; `end`: end the session).

requestId.description: The `requestId` when the payload correlates to a permission or control reply.

reply.description: What the session is sent when the rule fires.

wholeWord.description: Phrase mode only: refuse matches that sit inside a longer word.

ackedAt.description: When a turn last ended without matching the rule again, re-arming it.

fireCount.description: Fires in a row, each in a turn that matched again. Stops at {@link RULE_FIRE_CEILING}.

status.description: `pending` means fired, and no turn has since ended without matching it.

totalFires.description: Fires over the session's whole life, which re-arming does not reset.

scope.description: The sessions it is loaded into; absent is a linked document under `~/.claude/memories/`.

enabled.description:
A disabled hook is simply not written to any machine. Claude Code itself
has no way to disable one hook while keeping it, so this is cawco's
to provide: the row stays, the registration goes.

force.description: Set on a targeted push only: overwrite a machine copy that drifted.

hash.description: sha256 hex of the material a machine compares before writing.

id.description: Client-generated, like a rule's — the editor owns creation.

name.description: What the reader calls it. Unique across the fleet.

script.description:
A command hook's script body. CawCo writes it to a file on every machine
and points the registration at that path, so the hook travels — a machine
that has never seen this hook still runs it correctly. Absent means the
handler carries its own `command` and the reader is on their own for
getting that command onto each box.

cwd.description:
The checkout to write into. The hub fills this in as it sends a sync —
a daemon never resolves a project id, and a machine only ever receives
the project rows that live on it.

placeId.description:
The place (`project_places` row) this copy is for, on a copy the hub
placed: the machine reports what it came to under `<key>@<placeId>`, and
the hub folds every place's report back onto the row.

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. Required unless `user`.

scope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. MCP goes to `~/.claude.json`'s
  top-level `mcpServers`, skills to `~/.claude/skills/`, plugins install
  `--scope user`. The default, and what most rows want.
- `local` — one project, privately: `~/.claude.json`'s
  `projects["<cwd>"].mcpServers`, the map Claude Code already keeps per
  checkout and git never sees; plugins `--scope local`. What a
  project-bound row should be unless the reader asks to share it.
- `project` — one project, shared with whoever clones it: `.mcp.json` at
  the repo root, plugins `--scope project`. It writes inside the working
  tree, so it is never the default.

Skills have no `local` in Claude Code, so a project-bound skill lands in
`<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope.

kept.description: Where the moved credential is kept now, as its owner names it.

StreamServerMessage.description: Everything the stream protocol can put on the dashboard socket.

TranscriptBlock.description: One row of a transcript, as the hub built it.

id.description:
Stable for the life of the transcript, on every screen and after every
reload: the harness's uuid for the frame it came from (one assistant frame
is several blocks, `<uuid>:<index>`), a send's uuid, `task:<id>` for a
task line — and a hash of the frame for the few that carry no uuid.

metadata.description: Everything a renderer may need beyond `content`, keyed by the kind that uses it.

parentToolUseId.description: The Task call whose subagent said this. Absent on the main transcript.

queued.description: A send not read yet ({@link TranscriptPage.queued}).

sdkUuid.description: The harness's own uuid for the frame — the handle for rewind and fork.

state.description: A send's row: where its record stands.

timestamp.description:
When the turn happened, ISO-8601. A send: when the hub accepted it.
Anything else: when the harness stored its record. Absent when the
harness gives none — an invented clock would date a row by when it was read.

TranscriptBranch.description:
A subagent's branch: the Task call it hangs under, and how far it has got.
Its blocks are the blocks whose `parentToolUseId` is {@link toolUseId}.

lastEventAt.description: When the last branch event arrived, ISO-8601, for recency sorting.

model.description: Model that answered (wire id from assistant frames), or the requested alias until the first frame arrives.

taskId.description: The task the `task_*` progress messages report under.

toolUseId.description: The Task tool.use id that spawned this subagent.

TranscriptEvent.description:
One change to a transcript, in the order the hub made it. Applied in
sequence to the page a client fetched, it gives exactly the blocks the hub
holds.

busy.description: A turn is in flight, as the frames show it.

currentTool.description: The main loop's tool in flight, cleared by its result or the turn's end.

openBlock.description: Which content block the main loop has open right now, from the partials.

streaming.description: Partial assistant text of the main loop, between partials and the final message.

streams.description: Partial assistant text, per subagent branch, by its Task call id.

thinkingClosing.description: The SDK signed the thinking block: it is wrapping up, not still going.

thinkingSince.description: When the open thinking block started, epoch ms, by the hub's clock.

thinkingStream.description: What the open thinking block has reasoned so far.

commands.description: The `/` menu: names as the session lists them, which are skills, and their details once pushed.

harness.description: The harness the frames came from.

initialized.description: The transcript has turns in it: the session has already started.

inits.description: How many `init`s this transcript has seen since the hub built it.

lastCompaction.description: What the last compaction did, from the frames that reported it.

lastTurnFailed.description: The last turn came back an error — the SDK's `is_error`.

model.description: Which model answers the next turn, by the newest `init` or fallback.

permissionMode.description: How the session answers tool permissions, by the newest `init`.

sdkStatus.description: The session's own word on what it is doing: `compacting`, `requesting`, or nothing.

sessionId.description: The harness session key the newest `init` named.

tooling.description: The servers and tools the newest `init` announced.

totalCost.description: The cumulative cost the latest `result` reported, in dollars.

turnsEnded.description: How many turns have ended since the hub built this transcript.

TranscriptPage.description:
One page of a session's transcript, newest first. The newest page carries
the live state too, and the stream position it is consistent with: a client
subscribes with `afterSeq: seq` and applies the events after it.

blocks.description: The main transcript's blocks on this page, oldest first.

branches.description: The branches whose Task call is on this page, each with its blocks.

cursor.description: Pass as `before` for the page older than this; null at the conversation's start.

facts.description: Newest page only: what the session has said about itself.

queued.description: Newest page only: the sends waiting to be read.

seq.description: Newest page only: the stream position this page is consistent with.

tail.description: Newest page only: the live tail.

TranscriptStreamFrame.description: A transcript event batch, as it rides a session's Ledger stream.

Envelope.description:
Every message on every hop. `payload` is whatever the verb carries — a neutral
message, a harness option object, a control call — passed through. The hub
routes on the envelope fields and peeks only what harness.ts names.

requestId.description: The `requestId` when the payload correlates to a permission or control reply.

FramePayload.description:
`frames`: everything a session produces, flowing agent→hub→dashboard. The
`frame` kind is a neutral message; `raw` on it carries the harness's own
event verbatim.

SpawnPayload.description:
`spawn`: start a session on a harness. `harness` chooses the adapter (absent
means `claude`, for every caller written before harnesses existed); `options`
rides through to that adapter verbatim — only the callbacks the agent must own
itself (`canUseTool`/permission hooks, abort) are filled in on arrival, since
functions do not survive the wire. `resume` is the harness-neutral way to
re-open or fork a stored session; `persistSession: false` asks for a session
that is never stored (a spin-off's transcript).

account.description:
The account the session must run on, picked by whoever started it (the
dashboard, `delegate`, `start_session`). The hub refuses a pick the
session's machine, project or task does not allow, and never forwards
this field: what reaches the machine is {@link accountDir}.

accountDir.description:
The account the hub placed the session on, and so the store it runs
from on the machine: Claude Code in the account's own
`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/claude`, never the machine's `~/.claude`; pi on a
runtime whose `openai-codex` sign-in is the account's
`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/pi/auth.json`; OpenCode in the account's own
server, whose `XDG_DATA_HOME` (and so OpenCode's own store, holding the
account's credential alone) is `opencode-accounts/<id>` beside the
session credentials, hidden from every workspace boundary.
A launch learns it as it starts, from the hub's {@link LaunchGrant}, and
runs on that alone; a reattach is sent it, as the account its process
already runs on. Never set by a client. A Claude launch without one (or
a {@link homeLoginMove}) is refused on the machine; a pi or OpenCode
launch without one runs from the machine's own stores.

bootstrap.description:
Start from a repository instead of a directory that is already there: the
agent clones `repo` — `owner/name`, or any URL git understands — into a
subdirectory of `baseDir` and runs the session in the clone.

canDelegate.description:
Whether this session may spawn sessions of its own (`delegate` and
`start_session`). Set by the `delegate` tool's `can_delegate` param; a
delegate that is not granted it is a leaf: claude and pi never give it the
spawning tools, and the hub refuses any spawn naming it as parent. Absent
on a session nobody delegated (a mainline session may always delegate).

cawcoTodos.description:
"CawCo's to-dos" for this session whatever the fleet says: its delegate
type's `cawcoTodos`. The agent adds {@link cawcoTodosDenied} when this or
the fleet's choice is on.

delegateType.description:
The delegate type it was started as: its name, and the project whose
catalog it came from (none: the fleet's). The hub keeps both on the row.

denyTools.description:
Tools this session may never call, beyond whatever the harness already
denies. Set by a resolved {@link DelegateType}'s own `denyTools`; the
claude adapter merges it into the `disallowedTools` it already assembles.

effort.description:
How hard that model thinks, and how much it spends doing it. Hoisted for
the same reason again — and it is the third setting a `setEffort`
{@link ControlPayload} can still move mid-session. Named, it is the
session's chosen effort from then on ({@link InstanceRow.chosenEffort});
absent, the hub starts the process at the one already chosen, or, when
nobody chose, leaves the level to the harness, which is not the same as
asking for its default: only the model knows which stops it has.

fence.description:
This spawn is a project's memory curator or a fleet-watch triage run (a
`curator` or `overseer` row): the machine gives it CawCo's MCP server
and no other. Set by the hub alone, on every launch of such a row, and
never taken from a caller.

harness.description: Which harness runs the session. Absent = `claude`.

homeLoginMove.description:
The machine's own Claude Code login is moving into this account
(`POST /api/accounts/move-login`) and has not moved yet, so this Claude
session runs on that login: Claude Code with no `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, in
the machine's own store, where the credential still is. Granted by the
hub alone, as a Claude launch with no {@link accountDir} starts
({@link LaunchGrant}), and only while that move is pending. A machine
that has moved the login by the time the launch starts runs the session
in the account's dir instead.

ingested.description: Hub ingest cursor for a recovery sent after the registration handover.

instructions.description:
The fleet's role-scoped memory documents this session loads, in path
order: the hub picks them for its role and project as it grants the
launch ({@link LaunchGrant}), and the harness puts them in the session's
own instructions. Never set by a client; a reattach launches nothing and
keeps what its process started with.

keepAliveTurn.description: The in-flight maintenance send a surviving Claude process is answering.

lead.description:
This spawn is a project's Caw (a `lead` row): the machine puts each of
his shell and edit calls to the hub as a permission ask
(`LEAD_GATED_TOOLS`), whatever his mode, and answers none of them
itself; the hub's gate decides each (hub lead-gate.ts). Set by the hub
alone, on every launch of a lead row, and never taken from a caller.

model.description:
Which model answers, from the session's first turn. Hoisted for the same
reason as `permissionMode`. Absent leaves the choice to the harness.

options.description: Harness-specific spawn options, passed through verbatim.

parent.description:
The session that started this spawn (a delegate's parent, or the caller
of `start_session`): the child nests under it in every rail, and
`toolUseId` names the delegating tool call so the parent transcript can
render the round trip. Absent on a spawn a person asked for.

permissionMode.description:
How the session answers tool permissions. Hoisted out of `options` because
it is the one option the user keeps choosing — and the only one they can
still change afterwards, with a `setPermissionMode` {@link ControlPayload}.

persistSession.description: `false` asks the harness never to store this session's transcript.

processGeneration.description: Hub-owned launch identity, retained when reattaching a surviving process.

projectId.description: The project this session was started from, when it was started from one.

reattachOnly.description: Existing custody only: `busy` recovers active turns; `inspect` only reports them.

relaunch.description:
The process the session runs in is replaced, though the spawn resumes
its own conversation: it moves to another account, or starts again on a
permission mode its harness only takes at launch. Without it, a resume
for a session the machine carries is a recovery of that process, and
the process is kept.

requestId.description:
Correlates the `control_result` frame the agent answers the spawn with, once
the session is in place.

resume.description:
Re-open (or fork) a stored session. `sessionKey` is the harness's own
session id; `fork` reads the origin conversation into a new one; `atMessage`
resumes through that assistant turn in Claude; OpenCode reverts from
the selected user turn. A fork includes its anchor in either harness.

role.description:
The toolset the session runs in, written on its row at this first spawn
and kept there: a project's Caw is `lead`, a delegate type's `role` its
work item's. Absent: the hub derives it (`delegate` or `worker`).

scratch.description:
A spin-off (NEW.md §1): throwaway work. `worktree` runs the session in a
detached git worktree of `baseCwd` (the spawn's `cwd` when absent) so the
experiment cannot touch the checkout the mainline session is using.

scratchWorktree.description: Creation provenance, stored by the agent and carried durably on its hub row.

skills.description:
Skill names to load natively before the first prompt. Each harness loads
them via its own mechanism — opencode sends `/skill` commands, claude pushes
them into the input stream — so the delegate session sees the skill the same
way it would if the user had typed the slash command.

spawnedBy.description:
The session a hub job spawns for (a continuation's summariser and its
new session, on the person's ask): provenance for account placement,
not nesting. Unlike {@link parent}, it neither nests the child nor
routes reports, since no session started it.

title.description:
What the session is for, one line — a delegate's brief headline. Display
only.

workspace.description:
The workspace whose boundary every shell command of this session runs
inside. Set on each spawn of a work item's session — the first, and every
restore, revive and relaunch after it — and on no other session. A
machine that cannot hold the boundary refuses the spawn and says why.

StopPayload.description: `stop`: interrupt and close a live session.

claimedSessionIds.description: Addresses claimed by other rows; only unclaimed server runners make a legacy read ambiguous.

discard.description: Explicitly abort unadopted custody too, then tear down spin-off resources.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated stop claims as its caller; the hub honours the call only when the target is that instance's own delegate.

harness.description: Row-owned coordinates for ending server custody without adoption.

processGeneration.description: The row's launch identity, including a held process not yet attached.

requestId.description: Correlates the `control_result` frame confirming stop/discard or its failure.

scratchWorktree.description: Creation provenance, stored by the agent and carried durably on its hub row.

stopSequence.description: Connection-local hub order, echoed by reads begun after receipt.

ControlPayload.description:
`control`: invoke a named method on a live session, or on the machine when
`instanceId` is absent. The method is one of the neutral names in harness.ts
({@link CONTROL_INTERRUPT}, …) plus {@link RESOLVE_PERMISSION}; the reply
comes back as a `control_result` frame carrying the same `requestId`.

Machine-scoped, `method` names either a session-catalog operation — routed to
whichever harness owns the id (`harness`, or merged across all when listing)
— or a machine feature (`listRepos`, `installTool`, the fleet controls). With
no `instanceId` and no `harness`, `listSessions` merges every harness.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated control claims as its caller; the hub honours the call only when the target is that instance's own delegate.

harness.description: The harness the machine-scoped call is addressed at; session calls route by instance.

FsPayload.description:
`fs`: the machine's files, for the cwd picker and light markdown editing
(NEW.md §6) — not a file transfer. `list` answers with {@link FsEntry}[],
`read` with the file's text, `write` with the byte count it wrote, `media`
with an {@link FsMedia} — the one binary the tunnel carries, so a picture or
video an agent pointed at can be looked at without the agent spending tokens
on it.

content.description: `write` only: the text the file is replaced with.

path.description: Absolute; or, with `root`, relative to that root on the machine.

root.description:
`claude-home`: `path` is under the machine's user layer, Claude Code's
own dir (`~/.claude`), as the machine itself places it (core paths.ts
`claudeHome`): no caller has to know a machine's home to reach it.

FsEntry.description: One dirent of an `fs list`. `size` is 0 for a directory.

FsMedia.description: What an `fs media` read answers with: the file's bytes, base64, and what they are (a picture or a video).

SendPayload.description: `send`: one turn of input for a live session's prompt stream.

attachments.description:
Text the user pasted rather than typed, kept out of `message` so the agent
can fold it into the turn as quoted material the model won't mistake for
the sentence around it; and files, by the hub's reference, which the
agent fetches onto the session's machine and names by path in `message`.

delivery.description:
This hand-off of the send to its machine, stamped by the hub each time it
hands the send on. A machine handing the send back (`held_send`) names
it, so a hand-back a later hand-off overtook is not owed twice.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated send claims as its caller.

images.description: Images the turn carries: base64, with no `data:` URI prefix.

message.description: The user turn, under the uuid it keeps everywhere it is shown.

ReposResult.description:
What the machine-scoped `listRepos` control answers with. The GitHub CLI is
the machine's own credential store — cawco never holds a token.

UpdateReport.description:
What an {@link UPDATE_CAWCO} run did. Every field is what actually
happened, not what was asked for.

changed.description:
The services whose code the update changed: the only ones it rebuilt or
restarted, and the only way a deploy leaves the agent owing a restart.
Every service when nothing was pulled (an update asked of a current
checkout restarts the stack) and for a registry install.

pulled.description: The tail of what git said — 'Already up to date.' included.

skipped.description: Why something asked for did not happen.

NeutralSessionInfo.description: A stored session as the catalog lists it. `harness` says who owns the id.

ModelInfo.description: One model a harness offers. `value` is the wire id; `resolvedModel` the alias.

contextWindow.description:
The tokens one request to the model may send, as the harness reports it:
opencode's provider `limit.input` where it gives one, else its
`limit.context`; pi's `Model.contextWindow`; and for claude the
`modelUsage` window the hub last observed. Absent means unknown — never a
guess.

defaultEffort.description:
The effort the CLI applies when a spawn omits effort, measured by the
harness. Null when the model takes none; absent when not measured.

released.description: ISO date the model was released, when the catalog source says.

supportsEffort.description:
Whether this model has an effort scale, and which of its stops it reaches.
The pair is the *only* thing that decides what an effort control offers —
`xhigh` and `max` are model-dependent, and a hardcoded list of which models
have them is a list that is wrong by the next release.

SupportedCommands.description:
What {@link CONTROL_SUPPORTED_COMMANDS} answers, on every harness: the
session's `/` menu. A harness with no slash commands (pi) answers an empty
list, never nothing, so the menu reads one shape whoever answered.

AuthState.description:
Whether a machine's daemon can actually start sessions for a harness. For
Claude: whether any CawCo account is signed in on the machine.
`unreadable-credentials` is macOS's own failure: Claude Code keeps an
account's credentials in the login keychain, and a daemon outside the GUI
session is refused the secret (`errSecInteractionNotAllowed`). Generalized:
every harness reports its own auth word through the same three states.

NeutralTask.description:
One task of a session's plan, as every harness can express. Claude Code keeps
a ledger file per task; opencode has a native `todo` list; pi has neither.
The dashboard renders this one shape regardless of which answered.

priority.description: opencode's todos carry one; Claude Code's ledger does not.

at.description: When this was learnt, ms epoch.

detail.description:
`failed`: the tail of the installer's stderr. `unsupported`: what is
missing, named exactly — 'needs npm (Node 20+)' beats a grey chip.

method.description: The {@link ToolInstallMethod.label} that installed it or failed trying.

PreviewAddress.description:
Where a session's preview is served, as the hub reports it: its own port,
which the hub listens on in either mode, and in host mode the whole origin
the fleet's pattern names it by too. Which one a client loads is its own
choice, by where it reached the hub ({@link previewRoute}).

`host` is a bridge, not part of the address: host mode's `name[:port]`,
the only host-mode field readers built before `origin` (8c9b79c37) decode,
nightly 3146's dashboard and TestFlight 20261015 among them. Those readers
take `host` over `port`, so they open host-mode names as they did. Every
reader now reads `origin`. It goes in the change that expires TestFlight
20261015, once a TestFlight build that reads `origin` has shipped; the
wire check refuses it from the moment no shipped reader needs it (hub
scripts wire-compat.ts `BRIDGES`).

host.description: Host mode's `name[:port]`, beside `origin` alone: the bridge above.

origin.description: Host mode's whole origin for the session.

port.description: The session's own preview port, listened on in either mode.

PreviewTicket.description: A ticket into one session's host-mode preview origin: single-use, and spent by `expiresAt` (ms epoch).

HubAuthState.description:
What `GET /api/auth` answers: the mode, what this request is, and, for a
paired device, which one. Any client reads it to know whether it must pair.

device.description: The paired device this request came from; null for anything else.

CallerKind.description: What a request is to the hub.

HubAuthMode.description: Which way the hub admits callers.

PairingStart.description:
A client waiting to be paired (RFC 8628 §3.2's device authorization
response): what it shows (`userCode`), what it polls with (`deviceCode`,
kept by that client alone), how often, and for how long.

PairingRequest.description: A pairing waiting on the person, as every paired screen shows it.

DeviceKind.description: The kind of client a pairing is for.

OwnerDevice.description: A paired device, as `GET /api/devices` lists it. Its token never leaves the hub but once.

WaitingMachine.description: A machine that dialled the hub without a key's proof and waits for the person.

DelegateType.description: One named preset. `name` is the key a `delegate` call's `type` asks for.

account.description:
The account its sessions prefer, when placement allows it (the machine,
project and task allow it, and it is not benched or past its reserve).
Absent: the provider's strategy chooses.

canDelegate.description:
Whether a delegate of this type may itself delegate (or start sessions)
when the `delegate` call did not say. `false` (and absent) means a leaf —
the same default a bare `delegate` call gets; `true` makes the type a
coordinator by default. An explicit `can_delegate` on the call still wins.

cawcoTodos.description:
"CawCo's to-dos" for this type's sessions, whatever the fleet says
(§5.2, "changeable later in Settings and per delegate type"). Denied
lists only union, so a type can turn the choice on, never off: absent or
false leaves it to the fleet. A project type file says `cawco_todos: true`.

connections.description:
The connections (Projects spec §5.5) its sessions may call, by name: the
hub lists each one's tools to them as `conn__<name>__<tool>` and runs
every call itself, so no key reaches the session. A project type file
says `mcp: [x-brand]`.

description.description: What the calling model reads to decide whether this is the right type.

effort.description: How hard the model thinks: the same {@link EffortLevel} scale every other effort control uses.

name.description: Unique across the fleet; what a `delegate` call's `type` param names.

role.description:
The toolset its sessions run in ({@link SESSION_ROLES}): a project type's
`role:` (delegates/*.md). Absent: a delegate's.

TypeFileProblem.description: A file under `delegates/` that did not make a type, or a field one ignored.

CatalogType.description: One entry of a catalog, saying where it comes from.

budget.description: A type's spending limit: any of cost, turns and time, per a period.

brief.description: The type's brief: the file's body.

path.description: The file it was read from, inside the project folder.

shadows.description: A project type that replaces a fleet type of the same name.

DelegateBudget.description: A type's spending limit: any of cost, turns and time, per a period.

delegates.description: Use delegates instead of each harness's subagents.

deniedTools.description: The baseline as stored, the delegates choice and every other denial in it.

setAt.description: When someone last set the choices here (ms epoch); null while nobody has, so a new project's setup asks.

todos.description: Use CawCo's to-dos instead of each harness's own list and plan mode.

tools.description: What each choice denies, per harness.

upstream.description: Sessions may post to other people's repositories; null while nobody has answered.

path.description: The folder listed, from the root; `""` is the root.

truncated.description: True when the listing stopped at its cap before the last entry.

path.description: From the folder's root, `/` between parts.

FolderCommit.description: A write or delete as it landed.

changed.description: False when the content was already what was asked: no commit was made.

sha.description: The folder's commit after this change (HEAD).

path.description: The file, or `""` for the whole folder.

problems.description: Files in tasks/ the hub could not list as tasks, one sentence each.

stagesProblems.description: What is wrong with stages.md, one sentence each; empty when it reads.

TaskSummary.description: One task as a list shows it: the index's row, and what its attempts and edges say.

duplicateOf.description: The task it repeats (`duplicate_of`); null when none.

fields.description: The fields its file carries beyond a task file's own that hold one scalar (`priority: high`), as written.

foundIn.description: The task it was found in (`found_in`); null when none.

kind.description: The kind of its stage; null when its stage is not one of the project's.

needsYou.description:
It waits for you: its stage is of kind `you`, where only you move it on.
An attempt that failed or was stopped is its starter's business, not
yours. Derived on read, never stored.

outputs.description: The project folder files its work produces (`outputs:`).

problem.description: What in the file could not be read, or a stage the project lacks, in a sentence; null when all is well.

related.description: The tasks it is related to (`related`).

blockedBy.description:
The tasks it waits for (`after`) that are not done. Done: in a stage of
kind done, or dropped as a duplicate of a task that is done. A task the
project lacks counts as waited for, unless the folder's history shows its
file deleted or moved out of tasks/ (task-history.ts `goneTasks`).

lastAttemptFailed.description:
Its newest attempt failed, and it is not done or dropped since. The
failure is its starter's business (the session that started it, or the
lead for the dispatcher's), who hears the report: never the person's
Needs you. It keeps the task off the dispatcher's frontier until someone
starts or retries it.

lastAttemptStopped.description:
Its newest attempt was cancelled (stopped), and it is not done or dropped
since: no failure, and off the frontier as a failed one is. Who stopped
it is its attempt's `endedHow`.

liveAttempt.description: An attempt at it is starting or running.

queuedStart.description: Its stage's `runs:` hook asked for an attempt, which waits for a slot under the project's max_attempts.

startProblem.description: Why the hub could not start an attempt the last time it tried, while the task is unchanged since.

createdAt.description: When the commit that first added its file landed, ms epoch.

createdBy.description: Who made the commit that first added its file; null while no commit has it.

updatedAt.description: When its file last changed, ms epoch: its last commit, or an edit no commit has yet.

updatedBy.description: Who made its last commit; null while its file holds an edit no commit has.

archivedAt.description: When its file moved into tasks/archive/, ms epoch; null while it is not archived.

closeReason.description: The reason given with the move into the done or dropped stage it is in; null when none or open.

completedAt.description: When it moved into the done stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

droppedAt.description: When it moved into the dropped stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

startedAt.description: When it first moved into a stage of kind active, ms epoch; null while it never has.

TaskAttempt.description: One attempt at a task: a work item whose task it is, as a task read shows it.

endedAt.description: When it ended, ms epoch; null while it is live.

endedHow.description:
How it ended when it did not land, in a sentence the task shows beside
its Failed or Stopped badge: failed, the first line of what the hub
reported (`It failed without a reason.` when nothing was); cancelled,
`Stopped by <who>` (`Stopped` when the hub did not hear who). Null while
live and once done.

headline.description:
What its session said it did, in one or two sentences: its
`finish_item`'s headline. Null until an attempt finishes that way.

result.description: What its session handed in (`task_result`); null while it has not.

startedAt.description: When it was filed, ms epoch.

AttemptResult.description:
An attempt's result (`task_result`, hub task-tools.ts): what the session
that worked it says it did, what the reviewer should check, and what it
handed in, in the order it is drawn. One per attempt; a later call
replaces it. (A task's `TaskResult`, hub tasks.ts, is its newest
finished attempt's `finish_item` report.)

at.description: When it was handed in, ms epoch.

ResultArtifact.description: One thing an attempt handed in, as the review draws it.

name.description: What its chip says; left out, the file's name, the link's host or the artifact's id.

primary.description: The one the reviewer sees first.

WorkItemState.description: A work item's life. Only `starting` and `running` take messages.

id.description: The session's instance id (a session, the lead), or the approved action's id; null when the commit names none.

mover.description: The mover the change was checked as; null for a commit the hub's task code did not make (a hand edit, folder_write, the folder editor).

name.description: The commit's author: you, Caw, the session's title as it was, hub, approved action.

Tracker.description: Where a project's tasks live: CawCo's files, or (later) an outside tracker.

TaskView.description: One task, its file read whole, and what its attempts and edges say.

accounts.description: The accounts its attempts may run on; empty: every account.

budget.description: What an attempt may spend before the hub stops it; null: the project's default.

comments.description: Its `## Comments`, oldest first: each written by the hub with who and when.

context.description: Project folder files its attempt's brief carries (`context:`), the lead's pick.

duplicateOf.description: The task it repeats (`duplicate_of`); null when none.

extra.description: The fields its file carries that a task file does not know, with their values (a scalar or a list); kept as written.

group.description: Its attempts' group: their parent hears one combined report once all have ended.

hash.description: sha256 hex of the file as read.

kind.description: The kind of its stage; null when its stage is not one of the project's.

lands.description: Where an attempt's work lands, as the file says; null: the project's default.

needsYou.description: It waits for you: its stage is of kind `you` (see {@link TaskSummary.needsYou}).

owns.description: Globs of the repository's files an attempt owns.

result.description: What its newest finished attempt handed back; null until one has.

runsOn.description: Where its attempts run (runs-on.ts), as the file says; null: the project's.

sections.description: The body's other `## ` sections, as written.

blockedBy.description:
The tasks it waits for (`after`) that are not done. Done: in a stage of
kind done, or dropped as a duplicate of a task that is done. A task the
project lacks counts as waited for, unless the folder's history shows its
file deleted or moved out of tasks/ (task-history.ts `goneTasks`).

lastAttemptFailed.description:
Its newest attempt failed, and it is not done or dropped since. The
failure is its starter's business (the session that started it, or the
lead for the dispatcher's), who hears the report: never the person's
Needs you. It keeps the task off the dispatcher's frontier until someone
starts or retries it.

lastAttemptStopped.description:
Its newest attempt was cancelled (stopped), and it is not done or dropped
since: no failure, and off the frontier as a failed one is. Who stopped
it is its attempt's `endedHow`.

liveAttempt.description: An attempt at it is starting or running.

queuedStart.description: Its stage's `runs:` hook asked for an attempt, which waits for a slot under the project's max_attempts.

startProblem.description: Why the hub could not start an attempt the last time it tried, while the task is unchanged since.

createdAt.description: When the commit that first added its file landed, ms epoch.

createdBy.description: Who made the commit that first added its file; null while no commit has it.

updatedAt.description: When its file last changed, ms epoch: its last commit, or an edit no commit has yet.

updatedBy.description: Who made its last commit; null while its file holds an edit no commit has.

archivedAt.description: When its file moved into tasks/archive/, ms epoch; null while it is not archived.

closeReason.description: The reason given with the move into the done or dropped stage it is in; null when none or open.

completedAt.description: When it moved into the done stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

droppedAt.description: When it moved into the dropped stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

startedAt.description: When it first moved into a stage of kind active, ms epoch; null while it never has.

WorkBudget.description:
What a work item may spend before the hub stops it: dollars (the usage its
machine reports for its session), turns its session ends, and minutes of
wall time since it started. Each is optional; one reached fails the item.

TaskComment.description: One entry of a task's `## Comments`, written only by the hub (tasks.ts `comment`).

at.description: When it was written, ms epoch.

TaskCommentAuthor.description: Who wrote a comment, as its entry's heading says: the hub's actor.

id.description: The session's instance id, or the approved action's; null when none.

mover.description: The mover they wrote as (`you`, `lead`, `session`, …); null when the heading names none it knows.

name.description: The commit author's name: you, Caw, the session's title.

TaskResult.description:
What a task's newest finished attempt handed back, read whole on a task's
own read (never on the list: a report runs to pages): its session's report
of what it did, which is how an attempt presents its result whatever the
work, beside the outputs it handed in (`assets/<task>/`).

at.description: When the attempt finished, ms epoch.

headline.description: Its `finish_item`'s headline, one or two sentences; null when it gave none.

TaskTodo.description: One to-do of a task file (`## To-dos`), as a task read parses it.

id.description: Its marker, `td-3`; null on a to-do written without one.

path.description: Its position: `2` the second top-level to-do, `2.1` that one's first child.

promoted.description: The task it was promoted to (`tsk-152`), when its line ends in `→ #152`.

proposed.description: Offered by an attempt whose plan left it open (`(proposed)` before its words), not agreed yet.

text.description: The words after the box and marker, without the promoted link.

TaskHistory.description: A task's history as the API answers it: every commit to its file, oldest first.

path.description: Its file's path, or the last one it had.

state.description: `live`: on the board; `archived`: in tasks/archive/; `deleted`: its file deleted, its history kept.

TaskHistoryEvent.description: One commit to a task's file, as its history shows it.

at.description: When, ms epoch, by commit time.

path.description: The file's path once the commit was made: a rename's or an archive's new path.

reason.description: Why, when the change said: a close reason, the hub's cause (`attempt 5fd1e189 started`).

stage.description: The stage it went from and to; from is null for a new task. Null when the stage did not move.

what.description: What changed, in the commit's words: `stage draft → review`, `update title`, `tick td-2`.

TaskHistoryKind.description:
`created`: its file added. `moved`: a stage move. `changed`: fields,
to-dos or edges, through the hub. `commented`: a comment added through the
hub. `edited`: its file changed by a commit the hub's task code did not
make (a hand edit, folder_write); the hub putting back what one wrote
around it is `changed`, in words that say so. `archived`: its file moved
into tasks/archive/, or added there (a merged project's archived task);
`unarchived`: back out of it. `renamed`, `deleted`:
its file.

StagesView.description: A project's stages as the dashboard reads them.

decisionStarters.description:
What an empty Decisions tab offers to ask Caw for: the project's open
choices to lay out as a decision page (project-starters.ts), in that
order; none while Jev is off.

problems.description: What is wrong with stages.md, one sentence each; stages, moves and views are empty while there is any.

source.description: `file`: the project's stages.md; `template`: it has none, and the code template stands in.

template.description: The template the stages are, word for word, if any.

ProjectStarter.description:
One starter: a sentence the person would say to Caw, put in the composer
when pressed (nothing is sent), the glyph for its kind of work, why it is
offered, and what it comes from.

reason.description: Why it is offered: one plain sentence, at most 14 words and 120 characters, with no ids, slugs or shorthand (hub starter-asks.ts `reasonRefusal`); `sources` name what it comes from.

StarterSource.description:
One thing a starter comes from: a task id, a thread id, a folder path, a
commit sha, a routine id, or an event source and kind (`github:acme/site
issue.opened`).

StagesTemplateView.description: A template the dashboard offers: its stages, and the stages.md it writes.

ArtifactSummary.description: One artifact as the panel's list shows it, newest first.

promoted.description: Its last promote into the project's folder (`artifact_promote`, the doc's `meta.promoted`); null until one.

shownAt.description: When it was last brought to the front of the panel.

ArtifactKind.description:
The kinds of artifact (WORDS.md): HTML the agent wrote, a drawing, a dev
server or folder shown live, and a sheet: a story file's stories, each a
real component mounted by the project's own toolchain (core `stage.ts`).

ArtifactPromotion.description: An artifact's promote: the project folder's commit that holds it, and when.

host.description: Host mode's `name[:port]` beside `origin`: a bridge for readers before it (core `PreviewAddress`).

note.description: A canvas made with nothing to draw says so.

opened.description: Whether a view the person is looking at has it on screen ({@link Opened}).

origin.description:
A draft canvas's: its session's preview origin (core `PreviewAddress`),
where a client loads the canvas at `/__cawco/canvas/<id>/`: its port on
the hub's host, and (host mode) a whole origin of its own too, which a
client picks by where it reached the hub (core `previewRoute`).

route.description: Its live document on the hub's preview listener.

sheet.description: A sheet as its stage reads it: its stories with their args, its meta, and each component's props.

stage.description: A sheet's stage, or a served preview's server, as it stands once started.

why.description: Why it is not on screen, one sentence; only with `opened: false`.

wrote.description: The element ids a canvas's create wrote.

SheetRead.description: A sheet as its stage reads it: its stories, its meta, and the props of each component they mount.

ComponentDoc.description:
A component's props as the stage read them. `types` says how: `checked`
by the TypeScript checker or a docgen of its own, `jsdoc` from JSDoc
and PropTypes alone (the project has no TypeScript), `unknown` when
nothing could read them, with `note` saying why.

PropMeta.description:
One prop of a component as its framework's docgen reads it, in
Storybook's argTypes/PropertyMeta shape (spec §6): Svelte's by
svelte2tsx and TypeScript's checker, Vue's by vue-component-meta,
React's by react-docgen (react-docgen-typescript where a type is past
it).

defaultValue.description: Its default as the source writes it, like `"neutral"`; null when it has none.

options.description: An enum's values, or a token kind's names, in the order its type lists them.

PropKind.description:
A prop's type in Storybook's SBType names (`argTypes[name].type.name`),
which decides its control: `enum` the variant control, `boolean`,
`string` and `number` their fields, `slot` content that is a pin
(`Snippet`, `ReactNode`, a Vue slot), the rest read-only. A `token-*`
kind is a prop typed with one of the design system's generated token
types ({@link TOKEN_TYPES}): its options are the system's names.

SheetMeta.description: What a story file's default export says every story shares: its args, and the component each mounts unless it names its own.

component.description: The component, from the toolchain root; null when the meta names none the stage could resolve.

Story.description:
One named export of a story file: a story, by its export's 1-based place,
with its `args` as the file writes them. A literal arg (a string, number,
boolean, null, or an array or object of those) is its value; any other
(a fixture import, a function) is in `code`, its source text, and the
inspector shows it read-only.

code.description: Args whose value is code, not a literal: their source text.

component.description: The story's own component, from the toolchain root, when it names one apart from the meta's.

StageState.description:
A stage as the hub keeps it in each of its sheets' docs (`meta.stage`):
where it is, the toolchain root it runs (from the clone's root), why it failed
when it did, and the compile errors standing now.

dir.description: The toolchain root, from the clone's root ("." for the root itself).

message.description: Why it is in `error`, one sentence; none otherwise.

StageError.description:
A compile error the stage's Vite sent its pages, as the plugin keeps it
until the module compiles again: the module's file from the toolchain root,
1-based line and column when Vite's payload has them, Vite's message and
code frame, and the story files that import the module, which the hub
files it under.

sheets.description: The story files (from the toolchain root) whose sheet imports the module.

StageStatus.description:
Where a stage is: `starting` its first start, `waking` a start after
sleep, `live` serving, `error` it could not start or failed its restarts,
`asleep` stopped for want of a viewer, started again on the next open.

madeBy.description: The delegate that put it in this session's panel, when another session made it.

opened.description: Whether the person has had its latest revision on screen.

picks.description: A decision page's choices: how many it asks, how many are picked, how many picks are not sent yet.

picksAwaiting.description: Picks the person sent that the session has not read.

session.description: The session that made it, when it is not the caller's own (a lead reading its project's).

shown.description: Whether its session's panel shows it now.

unread.description: The person's changes (picks, notes, drawn elements) since the session last read it.

waitingOn.description: Whose move it is: the person's (shown and not opened since it changed, or a decision page's picks not made or not sent), the session's (sent picks or a canvas's changes unread).

changed.description: A canvas's elements the person changed since `since` (or since your last read).

changedUnderYou.description: A canvas's elements you replaced that the person had changed since your last read: "<id> changed under you".

deleted.description: Elements an update deleted, and the ids it named that the canvas does not hold.

draft.description: A canvas the person opened in the composer and has not sent yet.

edit.description: A sheet's write: the story file, from the clone's root, and the 1-based lines it changed.

outline.description: A canvas, as you read it: one line per element (core `canvasOutline`).

pictureAt.description: When the canvas's latest picture was drawn; null when it has none.

png.description: A canvas's latest picture, base64 PNG, when asked (`png: true`); null when it has none yet.

removed.description: Keys that changed since `since` and are no longer there.

sentText.description: What the page's `cawco.send(text)` sent with the person's last send.

seq.description: The cursor for the next read's `since`.

sheet.description: A sheet as its stage reads it: its stories with their args, its meta, and each component's props.

stage.description: A sheet's stage: its status, and the compile errors standing in the modules the sheet imports. A served preview's: its server's status, and why it is in `error`.

state.description: Every key, or with `since` only those changed after it.

workspace.description: A port preview's workspace, whose dev server it is.

wrote.description: The element ids an update wrote.

Removed.description: What `artifact_delete` and the panel's Remove answer: what the session's panel shows now, or null for nothing.

Found.description: A component the stage found (§6's discovery): its name, its file, and the story files that show it.

CommentRead.description:
What `comment_read` answers: each of the session's artifacts with pins
that match, the page's address the person last marked it at, and the time to
pass as the next `since`. A pin on ink carries the ink's box in the page.

address.description: The page's address the person last marked it at; its own route before any delivery.

elements.description: The page's elements under it (a comment: the one tapped); a canvas's, by id.

heard.description: What of it the session was last told ({@link pinSaid}); the hub stamps it on delivery.

ink.description: The stroke group it stands on, when it stands on ink.

movedAt.description: Its element is gone from the page since then; it waits in the moved tray.

number.description: In order of creation, per artifact, from 1.

point.description: Where on its element a tapped pin stands: fractions of the element's box.

sentAt.description: When it was first delivered to the session.

PageAnchor.description:
What a page's mark stands on: the element, by where it is written, its
selector and its text. An element inside a same-origin frame names the
frames it stands in, outermost first, each by its selector in the document
that holds it; its selector, source and text are read in the innermost
frame's document.

box.description: The element's box in the page when it was anchored, px: what the moved tray shows.

chain.description:
On a sheet: the components the element stands in, innermost first, each
where it is used (Svelte's `__svelte_meta.parent` component entries, or
a stamped component root's call site), then the story that mounts them.

frames.description: The frames it stands in, outermost first, each by its selector in its parent's document; none at the top.

sheet.description: On a sheet: its story file (from the toolchain root) and the story whose frame holds the element.

text.description: The element's text, at most {@link COMMENT_LIMITS.anchorText} characters.

ChainLink.description:
One link of a sheet's chain: a component, by its name, at the place it is
used (1-based line and column); the last link is the story, by its
export's name, at the export in the story file.

CanvasAnchor.description: A canvas's mark stands on one of its elements, by id.

PinnedElement.description: An element under a pin, as the overlay describes it, without its markup.

files.description: Files an agent's reply names as changed.

sentAt.description: When it was delivered to the session; a person's entry only.

Promoted.description: What `artifact_promote` answers: the project folder's commit, and the folder it wrote.

CanvasExport.description: A canvas's export: the `.excalidraw` file, its outline and its latest picture.

host.description: Host mode's `name[:port]` beside `origin`: a bridge for readers before it (core `PreviewAddress`).

origin.description: Its session's preview origin, where the canvas's page stands (`Created.port` / `origin`).

png.description: Base64 PNG; null until a screen has drawn one.

CanvasElement.description: An element as the outline reads it: Excalidraw's own fields, those it needs.

customData.description: Ours on Excalidraw's element: `shape` names what a held stroke was read as when Excalidraw has no type for it (a triangle).

graph.description: `decisions/decisions.json` is in the folder: the decisions form a graph.

problems.description: What could not be read, one sentence each.

DecisionPageSummary.description: A page as the Decisions tab lists it.

artifactId.description: Its artifact; null for a page whose artifact the hub no longer holds.

decided.description: Cards decided in its record; 0 before Make tasks.

tasks.description: Tasks filed from it ({@link DECIDED_FIELD} naming it).

updatedAt.description: When it was built, picked or sent last, ms epoch.

DecisionWriter.description: The session that wrote a page.

ended.description: It was ended: its person, parent or the hub stopped it, so Caw is woken instead.

GraphCard.description: One card on the graph: its page's card by id, and its place.

page.description: The page it is a card of.

picked.description: Picked on its page: derived on read, never written to the file.

DecisionPageRead.description: A page opened in the Decisions tab: its summary, its record and its last send.

sentAt.description: When the person last sent (I'm done picking, a comment), ISO; null before.

artifactId.description: Its artifact; null for a page whose artifact the hub no longer holds.

decided.description: Cards decided in its record; 0 before Make tasks.

tasks.description: Tasks filed from it ({@link DECIDED_FIELD} naming it).

updatedAt.description: When it was built, picked or sent last, ms epoch.

askedOf.description: The session asked to make its tasks; null when none was reached.

madeAt.description: When Make tasks wrote it, ISO.

RecordCard.description: One card of a decided page's record.

chosen.description: Options picked, by id; empty when it was left open.

dials.description: Its dials' values, in order: a panel named as the card.

note.description: The person's note; empty when none.

still.description: The mockup's still in the chosen state, by its mockup's built output; null when there is none.

DecisionOption.description: One option of a card, as the page labelled it.

keycap.description: Its digit in the card: the kit numbers options 1, 2, 3… in page order.

line.description: The line under its label; empty when it has none.

DecisionSent.description: What the hub answers a send on a page: who heard it.

threadId.description: The thread Caw was woken in, when he was.

pruned.description: The pairing is gone (401 or 410) and the device with it.

status.description: HTTP status, or 0 when Cawrier could not be reached.

ProjectOfferSummary.description: "Make this a project": offered once, on a plain session that outgrew itself.

line.description: One sentence naming why, ending in the question.

ProjectOfferReason.description:
What made the hub offer to make a plain session a project (project-offers.ts);
`caw` when nothing did: Caw proposed it in conversation and you said yes.

joined.description: True when the session's folder joined a project that already had its repository.

sessions.description: The sessions moved into it: this one, then its delegates.

setupThread.description: A new project's Setup thread, where its Caw sets it up; none when the folder joined one.

tasks.description: Plan items filed as proposed tasks, and the ones the project refused.

ThreadSummary.description: A thread as the project's list and the `thread.upsert` frame carry it.

hearing.description:
While his turn has read your words here and not yet answered them: what
he says in plain text after that send in his session is posted here as
his reply when the turn ends, so the thread draws it as he writes it.
Absent otherwise.

lastAt.description: When its newest message was added, ms epoch.

setup.description:
The project's Setup thread: the one New project opens with your prompt,
where Caw shows the setup page and lists what he wrote. Its replies that
name files offer "Open the board".

ThreadHearing.description:
Caw's turn answering your words in a thread, before his reply lands: his
session, and the send his turn read your words as.

ThreadStatus.description:
Where a thread stands, derived on every read and never stored: `working`
while the lead session is busy on a turn that thread woke, `needs-you`
while a question the lead asked in it is parked, else `ready`.

DesignOfferState.description: Where a project's design offer stands (`GET /api/projects/:id/design-offer`).

answer.description: `open` while unanswered; `built`: Build filed the task; `dismissed`: Not now.

SessionPlan.description:
What `GET /api/instances/:id/plan` answers, and what the live frames keep
a client's copy equal to.

source.description:
Where the steps come from: CawCo's own list (`todo_write`'s session
scope), when the session's native to-do tools are denied ("CawCo's
to-dos" on, and always on pi, which has none); else the harness's own
list (Claude Code's task ledger, OpenCode's todos).

spec.description: The session's spec, once it has written one.

taskId.description: On a task attempt: the task.

todos.description: On a task attempt: the task's to-dos, nested and ticked as its file has them.

PlanSpec.description: The session's spec, as it last wrote it.

PlanStep.description: One step of a session's plan: an ACP plan entry, with an id and a nesting depth.

depth.description: Nesting by indent: 0 for a top-level step, one more than its parent's for a sub-step.

id.description: Stable within one list: the writer's, the ledger's file number, or the step's place.

DispatchView.description: A project's dispatch: its settings, and what the dispatcher would do now.

budget.description: What an attempt may spend where its task and its delegate call say nothing; null: no limit.

dispatch.description: Whether the hub starts attempts at ready tasks on its own.

frontier.description: The tasks it would start next, in order.

lands.description: Where an attempt lands when its task and type say nothing.

leadInstanceId.description: The project's Caw session, once the hub has started one.

paused.description: Why it would start nothing now even with a ready task; null when it would.

queued.description: Tasks whose `runs:` hook start waits for a slot, oldest first.

runsOn.description: Where an attempt runs when its task says nothing (runs-on.ts); null: any machine with a checkout.

LandsMode.description:
Where a work item's work goes once it finishes (hub/src/landing.ts):
`main` onto the repository's default branch, `branch` to a branch of its
own on origin, `pr` to that branch with a pull request, `none` nowhere (the
work is not commits; its outputs are the deliverable).

AttemptStart.description:
An attempt as it started; or, `queued`, waiting for files a live item owns
(its ids null until it starts).

queued.description: Whether it waits for files a live item owns, to start when they are free.

stage.description: The stage the task is in now.

CawView.description: A project's Caw, as `GET`/`PATCH /api/projects/:id/caw` answer it.

answering.description:
What his turn answers when no thread woke it ("Answering a report from
site#4f2a"): shown on his panel, as no thread is working on it; null
when he is at rest or a thread's turn.

leadInstanceId.description: Caw's session, once the hub has started one.

model.description: The model Caw's session runs; null: its harness's default.

problem.description: Why Caw could not start now, on or off; null when he could.

running.description:
What Caw started that still runs, as his off control lists it, each lead
row followed by its delegates: the sessions his work items run, and his
own turn while an event started it. Turning him off with any of these
running asks whether they finish or stop; off, what still finishes.

spendUsd.description: Dollars every Caw session of the project has cost.

CawHarness.description: The harnesses a project's Caw can run on: the ones whose every shell and edit call the hub's gate decides.

CawRunning.description:
One thing Caw started that still runs: a session as a project's forget
lists it (project-stops `RunningSession`), and what it is.

kind.description: An attempt at a task, a delegate of his, or his own turn an event started.

offline.description: Its machine is not connected: it stops when its machine is back.

parentId.description: The nearest running row it is a delegate of; null for a top row.

title.description: Its name (a turn's: what it answers); null names it by its folder.

ProjectSpend.description:
What a project has spent, as `GET /api/projects/:id/spend` answers it, in
dollars, read now. Each part has one source: its Caw's turns as they were
booked (each turn's cost, from its result), its attempts' and other
sessions' usage as their machines reported it (a lead's sessions are not
counted twice). The parts add up: `monthUsd` is Caw's month, every
attempt's month and the others' month; Caw's month is its threads' month
and the turns no thread woke. Days and months are the hub's own (its
zone, as every "today" CawCo shows). What a project's cap counts.

attempts.description: Every task attempted this month, newest activity first: its attempts' month summed.
How many attempts the task has had.

lastAt.description: When its newest attempt was made or ended, ms epoch.

type.description: The delegate type its newest attempt ran, if one was named.

budget.description: What an attempt may spend where its task says nothing; null: no limit.

cap.description: The project's spend cap; null: it has none, and no limit.

caw.description: The project's Caw: its booked turns; `unthreadedMonthUsd`, this month's no thread woke.

fleetOnCap.description: What reaching a cap does when the project sets nothing: the fleet's default.

monthStart.description: The first of this month, ms epoch.

others.description: Every session of the project that is neither its Caw nor an attempt.

threads.description:
Each thread that moved this month, newest first: how many times it
woke Caw this month (your messages and events) and what those turns
cost (each turn's cost, booked to the thread that woke it).

ProjectCap.description:
A project's spend cap as it stands now: what the period has spent
against it, and what reaching it does. Spend is every session of the
project's (its Caw and its attempts) since the period began.

inherited.description: `onCap` is the fleet default, not the project's own.

onCap.description: What reaching it does: the project's own, else the fleet's.

reached.description: Spent at or past the cap. Read with `resetsAt`: past it, the cap is not reached.

resetsAt.description: When the next period begins, ms epoch; the cap counts from zero then.

startsAt.description: When this period began, ms epoch.

OnCap.description:
What reaching a project's spend cap does (Projects spec §5.3): `pause`
starts no new attempts at its tasks, `quiet` books what would wake its Caw
without a turn, `both` does both. The fleet has a default (Configure,
Spend); a project may set its own.

CapPeriod.description: The span a project's cap counts over, in the hub's own zone.

ThreadSaid.description: Your message as the hub took it: the thread (new or moved) and the message.

YourThreadMessage.description:
Yours: words you wrote, or your answer to the lead's question. An answer
carries `question` and `answer`, and `body` reads it in one line. Words
carry what rode with them as a send's do: `images`, and `attachments`
(pastes, and files by the hub's reference); Try again wakes Caw with all
of it.

answer.description: How you answered them: your choices, or that you walked away from them.

annotations.description: Per-question notes (preview selections), keyed by question text.

question.description: The questions the lead asked you in a thread (its AskUserQuestion).

UserAnswers.description: The reader's choices, back the way the tool reads them.

TextAttachment.description:
What a turn carries beside its typed words, other than pictures: a text
the reader attached or pasted at length, folded into the prompt as quoted
material; or any other file, which the hub stores (`POST /api/files`) and
the session's machine fetches and puts on its own disk before the harness
sees the turn, naming its path in one line of the message.

ref.description: The hub's reference to its bytes: `/api/files/<sha256>`.

ThreadImage.description:
A picture your words carried, in the hub's media store (media.ts): its
address there (`/api/media/<sha256>.<ext>`), as a send's row names it.

ThreadQuestion.description: The questions the lead asked you in a thread (its AskUserQuestion).

toolUseId.description:
The lead's call that asked them: the parked card on the thread's
composer settles into the answered row that carries it.

UserQuestion.description: One question of an `AskUserQuestion`-shaped prompt, as every harness can express.

CawThreadMessage.description:
Caw's, through `thread_reply`; `tasks` names the tasks it is about
(`tsk-12`), `files` the project folder's files it wrote (`stages.md`).

EventThreadMessage.description: Something that happened and woke Caw: a routine, an attempt landing, a task waiting for you.

body.description: What happened, opened like a fold; absent when the title says it all.

designOffer.description:
Caw asking whether to build a design system, with `event` null: the
ThreadEvent kind `design-offer`, held back as `routine-made` is.

event.description:
What happened, as typed data; null on a note stored before events were
typed, and on one whose kind is held back from it ({@link routineMade}).

phase.description:
`started`: a lead run woke Caw; `delivered`: a run's output;
`failed`: its second failure, which needs you.

slotLabel.description: The slot in words: "09:00" in the routine's zone, "test", "by-hand", "event", "inbox".

instanceId.description: The session the attempt ran in.

phase.description: `ended`: the attempt ended (`state`); `judge`: its acceptance criteria wait for Caw.

state.description: Its outcome, once ended; null while its criteria wait.

title.description: The task's title as the hub had it.

try.description: Which try at the task this was, 1 for the first.

stage.description: The stage of kind `you` it now waits in.

command.description: The command or file of one of Caw's gated calls; absent for a wake.

notWoken.description: Your words that did not wake him: on every `not-woken` event, and only there.

instanceId.description: The session fleet watch nudged about.

name.description: The session's name as fleet watch had it.

task.description: The task the sentence is about, and its title; null for none.

from.description: The offer or session the project was made from, in words; absent when it had none.

sha.description: Its commit; null for a change you declined.

what.description: Caw wrote it, or you answered his proposal for it.

noteTitle.description:
One line: source and what, like "Routine · Triage issues · 09:00". The
time is not in it: a reader draws `createdAt` in their own time zone.

routineMade.description:
A session made a routine, with `event` null: the ThreadEvent kind
`routine-made`, held back while an installable app reads `event` closed
(a bridge, hub scripts/wire-compat.ts BRIDGES).

DesignOfferEvent.description:
Caw asking first, once per project, whether to build a design system
(hub design-offers.ts): a design-shaped task entered an active stage in a
project with none. Build and Not now act on the project through
`/api/projects/:id/design-offer`.

sources.description: What the build would read, in words: "the repository's styles and components", "the brand kit".

taskId.description: The task whose move raised it.

RoutineSchedule.description: A routine's schedule as the person reads it: its cron in words, in its zone, and its next run.

nextAt.description: When the next scheduled run is due, ms epoch; null for a routine that is off.

ItemEnd.description: How an attempt or a delegate's work item ended.

CawNotWoken.description:
Your words in a thread that did not wake Caw (a `not-woken` event): why,
the hub's sentence for it, and your message he has not read, which Try
again (`POST /api/projects/:id/threads/:threadId/wake`) wakes him with.

message.description: Your message in the thread he has not read.

words.description: The cause, in the hub's words ("No machine is online, so Caw can't start.").

CawNotWokenReason.description:
Why your words did not wake Caw: `no-machine`, no machine is online for
him; `capped`, the project is past its spend cap; `could-not-start`, his
session could not be started; `place`, his place's boundary could not be
held on his machine; `not-taken`, his session did not take the message;
`failed`, anything else (its words say what).

by.description: `caw`: the project's Caw made it; `delegate` or `session`: another session.

expiresAt.description: When it turns itself off unless kept, ms epoch; null when it was kept as it was made.

why.description: What the making turn said just before the call, one paragraph; null when it said nothing.

sources.description: What the build would read, in words: "the repository's styles and components", "the brand kit".

taskId.description: The task whose move raised it.

RoutineMadeEvent.description:
A session made a routine with `routine_create` (routines.ts `announce`):
the notice in the thread its maker's turn was in, or the routine's own
thread when it was in none. Keep, Turn off and Open act on `routineId`
through `/api/routines/:id`.

by.description: `caw`: the project's Caw made it; `delegate` or `session`: another session.

expiresAt.description: When it turns itself off unless kept, ms epoch; null when it was kept as it was made.

why.description: What the making turn said just before the call, one paragraph; null when it said nothing.

ThreadRead.description: A thread and its messages, oldest first: `GET /api/projects/:id/threads/:threadId`.

ViewAsked.description:
"Ask Caw to change it" (`POST /api/projects/:id/views/:name/asks`): the
thread your words and the view went to Caw in, and whether he is on. Off,
he still answers your words (WORDS.md: "Off is never 'can't be
messaged'"); the page says so.

PhoneDone.description: What the hub did for a phone request.

RoutineView.description: A routine, as the routes and tools answer it (times in ms), with its newest runs.

madeIn.description: Where a session made it; null for yours, the hub's, and those made before the hub kept where.

madeWhy.description: What the making turn said just before its call, one paragraph; null when it said nothing or a session did not make it.

schedule.description: Its schedule in words, and its next run.

RoutineMadeIn.description:
Where a routine was made: the session whose `routine_create` call made
it, how its notice names that session, and the Caw thread its turn was in.

RoutineRunView.description:
One run, as the routes and tools answer it (times in ms), with what
actually ran it: a delegate run's work item, or a lead run's Caw session
and the thread its wake went to.

leadInstanceId.description: A lead run's Caw session, once his harness read its wake; null for a delegate run.

threadId.description: A lead run's thread: where its slot was noted and Caw woken; null for a delegate run.

workItemId.description: A delegate run's work item; null for a lead run, and before its work began.

RoutineRunState.description:
Where a routine's run is: queued behind a live run (an event's run, which
starts when the runs before it end), being started, running, ended, or
skipped (nothing started).

RoutineTarget.description:
What a run starts: a fresh delegate, a message to the project's Caw, or
the project's memory curator (memory.ts), a delegate in the `curator`
role that only the hub makes.

ConnectionView.description: A connection as every route and tool answers it: never its key.

account.description: Which account of the service it is, in the owner's words (`@brand`).

command.description: For `stdio`: the command the hub runs.

hasSecret.description: Whether a key or OAuth tokens are held for it.

header.description: For `header` auth: the header (or, for `stdio`, the environment variable) the key goes in.

projects.description: Projects whose every session may use it, beside the delegate types that list it.

reason.description: Why it is in `error` or `needs-sign-in`; absent when signed in.

tools.description: Its tools' names, as the hub last listed them; absent before a first listing.

ConnectionState.description: `signed-in`: its tools answer. `needs-sign-in`: a key or a sign-in is owed. `error`: `reason` says what failed.

IngressView.description: What a project's ingress is: its GitHub poller, routes, connector polls and newest events.

state.description: What is true of it, in a sentence: polled, or why not.

seen.description: Items its last call saw; null until its first call.

InboundVia.description: How an inbound event reached the hub.

GitHubCursor.description: Where one GitHub resource's poll stands: its ETag, its high-water mark, and its counts.

since.description: The newest `updated_at` taken in, ms: events at or after it are looked for.

lastDeliveryAt.description: When it last delivered an event to its routine; null when it never has.

RelayView.description: One relay as the hub answers it (times in ms epoch). Never its secret.

hasSecret.description: Whether a secret is set, and who made it: never the secret.

host.description: The machine whose Tailscale serves it: the hub's.

inbound.description: How events reach the project while it is or isn't live, in a sentence.

publicUrl.description: The public URL, once Funnel says it is live.

reason.description: The exact step or command when it isn't live; null when it is.

registered.description: Whether GitHub's webhook was registered by the hub (and is deleted with the relay).

testedAt.description: When the provider's test delivery arrived.

RelayCreated.description: What creating a relay answers: the relay, and the routes a lead may propose for it.

suggestedRoutes.description: Event routes for the project's routines, to propose to the owner (event_route_create), never made here.

ApprovedActionView.description: One approved action as the hub answers it (times in ms epoch).

account.description: The service's account the connection signed in as when it was proposed.

args.description: The call's arguments, JSON, exactly as it will be sent.

argsHash.description: SHA-256 of `args`, hex: what an approval names.

checkedAt.description: When you put a failed or unknown one away.

error.description: Why it failed, was refused, or is unknown.

projectName.description: The project's name, as the board names it.

proposedBy.description: The session that proposed it, and its title while the hub holds it.

result.description: What the service answered, JSON, cut at 16 KB.

routineId.description: The routine whose run proposed it (that run's session, or one it started); null outside any routine.

runAt.description: When it runs, at the earliest; null: as soon as it is approved.

runId.description: That routine's run; null outside any routine.

stageResult.description: What its stage move came to, once it tried.

thenStage.description: The task stage it moves to once done.

ProjectView.description:
A view as `GET /api/projects/:id/views` lists it: kept (`views/<name>.oui`)
or a draft (`views/drafts/<name>.oui`), its program as written, and the
components it names that CawCo's library does not have, which are left out
when it is drawn (the hub's parse, the same one the dashboard renders with).

dropped.description: Components the program names that the library does not have, by name: dropped, not invented.

ViewRemoval.description:
What removing a kept view does, in the hub's words, before it is done
(`GET /api/projects/:id/views/:name/removal`): the person's confirm on
the block or the tab says this.

ask.description: The question the confirm asks: what goes, and the block it leaves.

file.description: The view's file, deleted as a commit.

page.description: The page it stands on as a block, or null: it is its own tab.

ViewRemoved.description: A kept view removed (`DELETE /api/projects/:id/views/:name`): what went.

commit.description: The commit that deleted its file.

page.description: The page whose block it was, or null: it was its own tab.

said.description: What went, in the hub's words.

ViewTaskRow.description: One task as the `tasks` tool answers it: the board's row, and its dates.

byKind.description: Tasks in a stage of each kind.

stages.description: The project's stages, in the order its stages file names them.

ViewRoutine.description: One routine of the project, with its newest runs.

target.description: A fresh delegate each run, a message to Caw, or the project's memory curator.

outcome.description: How it ended: `delivered`, `silent`, `failed`; null while it runs or when it was skipped.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or queued, or how it failed.

slot.description: `test`, `by-hand`, `event`, `inbox`, or the time of its scheduled slot in the routine's zone ("09:00").

byRoutine.description: Each routine of the project: what its runs in the window spent, and how many there were.

byType.description: Each delegate type the project's delegated work ran on in the window (null: none named), and its items.

ViewEvent.description: One inbound event from outside (GitHub, a polled connection).

handledAt.description: When a routine took it, or null while none has.

kind.description: What kind of event it is (`issues.opened`, `pull_request.closed`, a connector's kind).

routedTo.description: The routine a route sent it to, by name; null when no route took it.

source.description: Where it came from (`github`, a connection's name).

BlockArrangement.description:
A project's arrangement, as `GET /api/projects/:id/blocks` answers it:
each page the person has arranged, its blocks in order, and the drafts
standing on a page as proposed blocks. A page never arranged is absent,
and shows its built-in blocks in their own order.

BlockPlace.description: One block in a page's arrangement.

hidden.description: Folded off the page; it keeps its place and comes back from the page's end.

width.description: Narrow takes the columns its measure needs; wide spans the row.

ProposedBlock.description:
A draft view standing on a page as a proposed block: where it asked to
