stand, and who drafted it. Keep places it there; Remove discards the
draft. It is no tab while it stands.

by.description: Who drafted it: "Caw", or a session's name.

position.description:
Its place in the page's order (every block of the page, hidden ones
included, counted from 0), or null: the page's end.

addresses.description: Tailscale first, then every non-internal IPv4 the hub's machine has.

sshPublicKey.description: The public key the hub's SSH adds sign in with, or null when it has none.

JoinAddress.description: One address a machine could reach this hub on.

label.description: Where it came from: `Tailscale`, `Tailscale DNS`, or an interface name.

url.description: `http://host:port`, the hub's REST base as seen from that address.

SshJoinJob.description: `GET /api/machines/ssh/:id`: one SSH add, as the hub holds it in memory.

lines.description: Everything the SSH session printed, stdout and stderr in arrival order.

machineId.description: From the `joined as` line, once it has been printed.

state.description: `done` means the script exited 0 and the hub has the machine online.

BinaryUpdatePolicy.description: Browser-neutral release policy and machine state consumed by API clients.

autoUpdate.description: One setting for the whole fleet: a machine does not pick its own.

BinaryUpdateChannels.description: What the hub knows of each channel; `null` where the release host has no release.

checkedAt.description: When the release host was asked, in milliseconds.

ChannelRelease.description: The newest signed release of one channel, as the release host shows it.

schemaVersion.description: Database migrations this build carries; a build with fewer than the database holds is never installed.

sequence.description: First-parent commit count of the built commit; only grows, and no path installs a lower or equal one.

sessiondProtocol.description: The capability required by this build's agent from its process keeper.

WorkflowListing.description:
A workflow as the list carries it: everything but its program, which only
the workflow's own read serves. The graph stays: the editor resolves a
called workflow's Start inputs from it, and the app's launch form reads it.

graph.description: The editor's model. Null for a program written by hand or by an agent.

inputs.description: The program's `inputs` export, as the launch dialog and stubs need it.

state.description: A template; text that parses as a JSON object or array goes as structured state.

effort.description:
How hard the model thinks, and how much it spends doing it: Claude Code's
effort scale, in its own order. Hand-written rather than tunnelled from the
SDK — nothing in this file imports a harness SDK, and `@cawco/core` has no
dependencies at all — but it is the SDK's `EffortLevel` verbatim, so the
claude adapter hands it straight on.

Effort is not only thinking depth. A lower level also buys fewer and more
consolidated tool calls, less preamble and terser confirmations; a higher one
spends tokens in all of those places. A harness with no such knob reports
`effort: false` rather than mapping onto this.

JevNodeQuestion.description:
One question on a Jev node, as the editor holds it. Choice options are rows
(name + meaning) so a half-typed option can exist while it is edited; the
compiler turns them into the API's `{ name: meaning }` criteria.

WorkflowRunSummary.description:
A run as a workflow's run list carries it: what the clients' lists read,
none of its graph, inputs, result, state or log. The rest is the run's own read.

seenAt.description: When the owner last looked at it or archived it, on any device.

WorkflowAsk.description:
The question a `waiting` run is parked on. Self-contained on purpose: a
code-origin run has no graph to read the question off, so the hub sends the
whole thing, on the run detail and on the frame that announces the wait.

answerSchema.description:
JSON Schema for a typed answer, when the program gave `w.ask` an `answer`
schema: the answer then carries a `value` validated against it.

WorkflowEffectKind.description: Every effect kind the bridge can carry: one `w.*` call.

WorkflowFailure.description: How a typed rejection crosses the worker boundary and comes back.

AgentRow.description:
A machine from the hub's `agents` table — what `GET /api/agents` answers with,
and what rides alongside the sessions in an `instances` frame.

auth.description: `unknown` until a daemon that probes has registered at least once.

build.description: The cawco build this machine's daemon is running (NEW.md §12).

custody.description: Last register's sessiond read, distinct from an available empty list.

harnesses.description: What each installed harness can do, as the daemon reported at register.

home.description: The machine's home folder, absolute, as its daemon reported at register; absent until one that says so has.

lastSeenAt.description: A `Date` inside the hub, the ISO string it serialises to everywhere else.

pausedUntil.description:
The owner paused the machine until this time (epoch ms): CawCo starts
nothing on it until then, though its agent stays connected. Null when it
is not paused.

pauseStopped.description:
What the pause stopped as it began, as said ({@link stoppedWords}):
"stopped 1 running check". Null when it stopped nothing, or is not paused.

tools.description: Last-known workflow-tool status by tool id (NEW.md §10).

commands.description:
The ids of the last Install now commands this machine acted on, oldest
first: one delivered again is answered and not acted on twice.

cut.description:
What the last install cut: the work in flight when it was applied anyway,
because a person pressed Install now or auto-update had waited its cap.
Kept until the next install.

failedVersion.description: The build that failed to come up and was rolled back; not retried by itself.

heldChildren.description: Children a keeper the new build cannot speak to holds, while they are the reason for waiting (`waiting-sessions`).

hostsHub.description: True on the machine that runs the hub.

keeperFailedVersion.description: The build whose session keeper could not start; the keeper is not handed to it again by itself.

keeperRestart.description:
The last time the agent found a session keeper wedged (alive, socket
open, no welcome) and restarted it, or (`retiring`) removed it, which
ended every session it held. The event a notice announces, as
`keeper:<machineId>:<at>`; the next one replaces it.

at.description: When the wedge was called, in milliseconds: the restart's identity.

children.description: Processes the keeper held, each a session or a helper, ended with it.

diagnostics.description: Where what the keeper was doing was saved, on that machine.

dials.description: Dials in a row that got no welcome.

retiring.description: It was a retiring keeper (an earlier build's, after a handover), removed rather than restarted: no session starts on it again.

silentForMs.description: From the first silent dial to the call.

landed.description: The last install or rollback that finished.

retiringKeepers.description:
Keepers of earlier builds still holding sessions after a handover, each
with how many: every new session starts on the current keeper
(`sessiondVersion`), and each of these exits once the last session it
holds has ended or gone to sleep. Absent when there is none.

sessiondVersion.description: The build of the current session keeper, the one every new session starts on: the `keeper` link.

updatedAt.description: When anything in this state last changed. Not an identity for anything.

waitingOn.description: What `ready` waits for: the work in flight a restart would cut now.

waitingSince.description: When auto-update first waited on work in flight; it installs anyway once its cap has passed.

RestartHold.description: One kind of work a restart would cut now, and what each piece is (a session, a call).

RestartHoldReason.description:
Kinds of work a restart of the agent or the hub would cut. A turn is not one:
the session keeper runs it, and the next agent takes it over where it stands.

- `custody`: the agent is still taking over the sessions the keeper holds.
- `starting`: a session start the agent is in the middle of.
- `image`: an image generation the agent is running.
- `workspace`: a delegate's workspace the agent is cutting or archiving.
- `command`: a command the hub asked the agent to run (a landing gate step, a workflow step).
- `tool-call`: a tool call the agent relays to its hub.
- `hub-tool-call`: a CawCo tool call the hub is answering, from any machine.
- `write`: a message or an answer the agent is handing to a harness.
- `opencode`: an OpenCode server operation the agent runs (a config apply,
  a session opening, an MCP change, a handoff between server generations).
- `opencode-send`: messages the agent holds for OpenCode, not yet handed over.

BinaryUpdateLanding.description:
The last install or rollback that finished. It is the event a notice
announces, so nothing but the finish of an install or rollback sets it, and
the next one replaces it: the state's other writes carry it through
unchanged, and the session keeper moving to the build later is part of the
same update, not a new one. Whether a person has seen it is the hub's
record (`POST /api/notices/seen`, as `landed:<machineId>:<at>`), so one
acknowledgement holds for every tab and device.

at.description: When it finished, in milliseconds: the landing's identity.

version.description: The build installed, or the build that failed and was rolled back.

RetiringKeeper.description: A keeper of an earlier build still holding sessions while the current one takes every new start.

sessions.description: Its sessions, and any other process it holds (a workspace's boundary, an OpenCode server).

BuildInfo.description: What a daemon reports about the checkout it was started from.

commit.description: Short git SHA, when the checkout is a git one.

dirty.description: Whether that checkout has uncommitted changes.

startedAt.description: When this daemon started, ms epoch.

FleetSyncReport.description:
A machine's answer to `syncFleetConfig`, and what `agents.fleet` stores:
every desired entry, by the same keys the config used.

at.description: When the sync ran, ms epoch.

have.description:
What this machine holds on its disk once the sync is done, by hash — the
content-carrying rows only, hashed as the hub hashes them. It tells the
hub whose content moved, so running sessions reload. Which bytes a sync
leaves out is never decided from it: the hub reads the disk again
({@link READ_FLEET_HOLDINGS}) just before every sync.

hooks.description:
The fleet's hooks, by the same id the hub keeps them under. Absent from a
daemon that predates them. `failed` covers three different machine-local
facts — a hand-edited script, a validation the hub already passed but this
row failed again, or a project hook with no checkout here — and `detail`
is what tells them apart.

mcpByHarness.description: Per-harness runtime truth, before the machine row's worst-state aggregation.

memoryDocs.description:
The linked documents, by the same path the set keyed them under. Absent
from a daemon that predates the set; one drifted document says so on its
own row, with the main file still `applied` beside it.

memoryHook.description:
The model-memory SessionStart hook an earlier cawco registered, while a
machine has not managed to take it back (agent fleet.ts
`retireMemoryHook`): always `failed`, with why. Absent once it is gone.

skills.description: Absent from a daemon that predates directly-fetched skills.

toolchain.description:
The CLIs this sync leaned on, so a failure can be attributed to a binary
rather than to the machine as a whole. Absent from a daemon that predates
it, and from one that found nothing to report.

FleetItemState.description:
What one desired entry came to on one machine. `removed` is a success: the
row was disabled or deleted and the machine no longer has it — reported
once so the dashboard can say so, gone from the next report.

detail.description: `failed`: what the write or the CLI said — the tail of it.

FleetToolchain.description: The CLIs a machine's sync leaned on, by the name they are known under.

claude.description: Every `claude` this machine has; the one the sync ran is marked `used`.

CliInstall.description:
One install of a CLI a sync depends on, as the machine found it.

The reason this exists: a machine may carry several `claude` binaries at
once (a homebrew one, an npm-global one, the local installer's), PATH picks
whichever comes first, and a CLI too old for a flag the sync passes fails
with a sentence that names neither the binary nor its version. Reporting the
install makes that a fact on the dashboard rather than an expedition.

path.description: Absolute path of the executable, resolved through any symlink.

used.description: Set on the one the sync actually ran — the binary a failure came out of.

version.description: What `--version` said, when it would say.

HarnessReport.description: What a machine knows about one harness: is it installed, can it work, what can it do.

accounts.description:
Claude only: every account's config dir on the machine
(`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/claude`) and what `claude auth status` said of
it there. The hub reads it as where each account is signed in. The
machine's own `~/.claude` is never read.

authReason.description:
Why a session of this harness cannot start here, without credential
data: pi's sign-in unavailable or unchecked, or OpenCode's server
refusing to start (and not tried again until its inputs change). The
home says it as this machine's word.

modelNames.description:
pi only: the model each bare model id pi offers resolves to, by pi's own
resolver (`resolveCliModel`) with this machine's accounts counted as
signed in, as `provider/id`. A name pi cannot resolve is absent. The hub
reads the provider, and so the account, of a session started on one of
them here. `default` depends on the session's directory and is asked
per start ({@link CONTROL_PI_DEFAULT_MODEL}).

models.description:
The models this harness offers on this machine.

It rides the machine's report for the same reason {@link * HarnessCapabilities.permissionModes} does, and not the {@link * CONTROL_SUPPORTED_MODELS} control beside it: the catalog is a property of
the installed CLI and the account behind it, identical for every session on
the machine and knowable with none running. Asking a session for it made a
fleet-wide fact inherit one session's lifecycle — a machine with nothing
running had no catalog at all, so its model picker was empty and no session
could be named or shown an effort scale.

Absent (not empty) from a machine whose agent predates the field, and from
a harness that could not be probed; empty means it was asked and offered
nothing.

signInFaults.description:
OpenCode only: each of the machine's own OpenCode sign-ins (not a CawCo
account) whose provider refused it the last time a session here used
it, until a turn on that provider succeeds. The home says each on the
machine's row, with the fix ({@link opencodeSignInFaultWords}).

unreadAccounts.description:
Claude only: the account dirs (`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/claude`) Claude
Code gave no answer for on this read: its `auth status` ran out of time
or printed nothing it could mean. Neither signed in nor out: the hub
keeps what it last had for each, and does not read them as gone.

version.description: The CLI/SDK version, when it can be read.

AccountReport.description:
What one account's store on a machine says: whether it is signed in, how,
and as whom. Claude: `claude auth status` in the account's config dir.
Any other provider: the credential in the account's `credential.json`, its
identity read there (a ChatGPT token's claims, a key's fingerprint). Read
on every connect and again every minute, so a store signed in as someone
else since is seen within a minute. A Claude account's models are the
hub's to ask ({@link CONTROL_PROBE_ACCOUNT}), once per account.

account.description: The account whose store this is, under `~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/`.

identity.description: Who the store is signed in as. Absent when it names nobody.

kind.description: `console` for a Claude Console login; `oauth` or `api_key` for any other provider's credential.

provider.description: The provider of the credential held; absent for a Claude dir.

AccountIdentity.description:
Who an account is. Claude: as Claude Code's initialize response reports it
(`account.email`, `account.organization` — the organization's name).
ChatGPT: the access token's claims, read on the machine — the email
(`https://api.openai.com/profile`.email) and, as `organization`, the ChatGPT
account id (`https://api.openai.com/auth`.chatgpt_account_id), the
workspace the subscription bills. Another OAuth provider: the email its
credential names, if any, and its provider id. A key: its last four
characters (`…a1b2`) and, as `organization`, a fingerprint of it
(`key:` and the first 16 hex of its SHA-256), so the same key on two
machines is one account and the key itself never leaves them.

HarnessCapabilities.description: What a harness can do, so the dashboard gates features instead of guessing.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort scale, at spawn and mid-session.

fleet.description: The harness applies the hub's fleet config (MCP/skills/memory/agents) to its own files.

fork.description: Fork a stored session into a new one.

tagSession.description: The scratch-tag the catalog filter reads.

PermissionMode.description:
How a session answers tool permissions. The union is Claude Code's, plus
`fullSend`, CawCo's own: Claude Code's `bypassPermissions` with the host
also answering the safety checks the CLI still raises in that mode. Each
adapter maps `fullSend` onto its harness; none hands it to an SDK as is.

HarnessKind.description: The harnesses cawco can spawn sessions on. Adding one is a new adapter.

EffortLevel.description:
How hard the model thinks, and how much it spends doing it: Claude Code's
effort scale, in its own order. Hand-written rather than tunnelled from the
SDK — nothing in this file imports a harness SDK, and `@cawco/core` has no
dependencies at all — but it is the SDK's `EffortLevel` verbatim, so the
claude adapter hands it straight on.

Effort is not only thinking depth. A lower level also buys fewer and more
consolidated tool calls, less preamble and terser confirmations; a higher one
spends tokens in all of those places. A harness with no such knob reports
`effort: false` rather than mapping onto this.

SignInFault.description: One of a machine's own sign-ins its provider refused ({@link HarnessReport.signInFaults}).

at.description: When the refusal came, epoch ms.

provider.description: The provider's id in the harness (`anthropic`).

words.description: What the home says, whole: what was refused, and the fix ({@link opencodeSignInFaultWords}).

MachineCapability.description: Optional machine tools. Reporting never installs or impersonates a tool.

installCommand.description:
What installs it here. Empty when nothing may: a copy came some way
CawCo has no method for, and another would be a second copy (`reason`
says so).

ContinuationJob.description:
A continuation in a new session the hub is carrying, as every dashboard
follows it: the source files its open items (a person's Continue), is
summarised, then a new session starts seeded with the summary and those
items. The hub owns it from the POST that starts it to its end; its Cancel
(`DELETE /api/continuations/:id`) stops it in any stage before `started`.

inPlace.description:
Never sent: no job goes on in place now. Declared only because the
TestFlight builds 20261015 and 20261015.3 read it, which the hub's wire
check holds to (packages/hub/scripts/openapi.ts); it goes in the change
that expires them.

stage.description:
`filing`: the source's turn filing its open items (a person's Continue);
`starting`: the new session is starting.

summariserInstanceId.description: Absent when the source is short enough that nothing is summarised.

MoveEstimate.description:
What the New session modal reads when a machine without the project is
picked: `GET /api/projects/:id/move-estimate?machine=<target>[&path=]`.

ask.description: What "Move it" does, for New session's step 2; set when a move is needed and can run.

display.description: The destination as the person reads it, under the machine's home as `~`: `~/cockpit`.

lfsBytes.description: Bytes of large files after the clone.

needed.description: Whether a move is needed: false when the target already has a checkout place.

needsApproval.description: Whether `approval` is a step: no repository yet, or files over 50 MB would go raw.

path.description: The destination: the place it has there (`needed: false`), else where it would go.

refused.description: Why it can't move, as the modal's reading line says it.

uncommittedFiles.description: Files with uncommitted changes on the source (tracked and untracked, not ignored).

MoveAsk.description:
What a move does, as the person reads it before "Move it" (the owner's
pick D "Plain + details"): in New session's step 2, which the modal
morphs to on "Move & start", and on the approval card of a move started
anywhere else.

bigFiles.description: The large files that go to LFS with the yes.

details.description: The Details fold: the git terms of what "Move it" runs, one per line, for mono.

gitInit.description: The folder is no repository: "Move it" runs `git init` and one commit.

key.description:
What the person says yes to, when the move needs a yes (the folder is
no repository, or big files would go into history): New session sends
it back as {@link MoveRequest.approved}. Absent when no yes is needed.

lines.description: The lines under the title, in order.

MoveLargeFile.description: One file of a job's approval ask that goes to LFS: its path and size.

MoveJob.description:
A move job as every dashboard and the apps follow it: on the `moves`
frame, in the `instances` frame's `moves`, and at `GET /api/moves`.

ask.description: Set when `approval` is a step: what "Move it" does, for its card and its step's words.

askId.description:
While `approval` waits on a yes nobody gave in New session (a
delegate's, a task's or the API's move): the ask parked through the
same channel as every permission ask (dashboards, push, Telegram), on
the session's own row ({@link targetInstanceId}, which reads "Needs
you"), an `AskUserQuestion` whose options are "Don't move" and "Move
it", answered like any question at `/api/pending`.

bytes.description: Bytes the clone fetches, as the source's repository measured them.

error.description: A job's failure: the step it failed at, in words, and the tool's own last line.

from.description:
Where the clone comes from: the hub (a project with no outside remote)
or the project's outside remote, by host ("github.com"), which names the
step ("Fetching from GitHub").

install.description: Set while `install` is a step: the command the target runs.

kept.description: What a Cancel left on disk, in words, once cancelled.

lfs.description: The large files: how many, and their bytes; set when `lfs` is a step.

lfsFile.description: While a file of at least {@link LARGE_FILE_BYTES} is in flight: the largest one.

moved.description: Once started: what moved, for the ready line ("cockpit to obelisk · snapshot cawco/move/gearbox").

progress.description: Bytes so far of the step in flight (`clone`, `lfs`).

snapshot.description: Set when `snapshot` is a step: the branch the hub holds the work on, and how many files were uncommitted.

stayed.description: Once started: what stayed, for the ready line ("your .env and ignored files stay on gearbox").

steps.description: The steps this job runs, in order: the pane draws the ones ahead muted.

stoppedAt.description: Once cancelled: the step it stopped at.

targetInstanceId.description:
The session the job starts, under this id from the start: its row is on
the board from then (status `moving`, named by its New session title or
its first prompt's words), and the start takes the same row on.

MoveError.description: A job's failure: the step it failed at, in words, and the tool's own last line.

detail.description: The tool's own last line (git's, the installer's), any credential removed.

MoveStep.description: A stage the job does work in.

MoveInstall.description: What `install` runs, chosen by the lockfile at the repository's root.

command.description: The command as one line, for the pane's mono subline: `bun install`.

MoveStage.description: Where a job stands: at one of its steps, or settled.

MachinePath.description:
An absolute, normalised path on one machine (see the module). On the wire
it is a plain string: the brand is the compiler's alone.

ConfigInspection.description:
What a session started in `cwd` would actually see, and what a machine has
outside any project when `cwd` is absent. The answer to two questions the
dashboard asks: "what is on this machine that cawco does not manage?" and
"what will this folder give me?" — asked the moment a folder is chosen.

memory.description:
The machine's own user CLAUDE.md, or null when it has none. `managed` says
cawco wrote what is there — an unmanaged one is worth adopting. `docs`
is whatever the machine has under `~/.claude/memories/`, read the same way
and absent from a daemon that predates the set.

DiscoveredMcp.description:
One MCP server a machine really has, wherever it came from. What
{@link INSPECT_CONFIG} reports — the fleet's own rows included, so a reader
sees one list rather than two halves of one.

managed.description: Whether cawco wrote it — an unmanaged row is one worth adopting.

shadowedBy.description:
Set when a nearer scope defines the same name and wins. Claude Code's own
precedence is local > project > user, and a fleet server quietly shadowed
by a checkout is the kind of thing a reader should be told, not debug.

FleetMcpConfig.description:
A serializable MCP server definition — the SDK's own config shapes minus the
in-process `sdk` kind, which cannot cross a wire. Stored verbatim in the
hub and written verbatim into `~/.claude.json`; `${VAR}` expansion inside
is the CLI's own affair.

McpStdioServerConfig.description: MCP server config shapes, re-declared so `fleet.ts` stops importing the SDK.

FleetScope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. MCP goes to `~/.claude.json`'s
  top-level `mcpServers`, skills to `~/.claude/skills/`, plugins install
  `--scope user`. The default, and what most rows want.
- `local` — one project, privately: `~/.claude.json`'s
  `projects["<cwd>"].mcpServers`, the map Claude Code already keeps per
  checkout and git never sees; plugins `--scope local`. What a
  project-bound row should be unless the reader asks to share it.
- `project` — one project, shared with whoever clones it: `.mcp.json` at
  the repo root, plugins `--scope project`. It writes inside the working
  tree, so it is never the default.

Skills have no `local` in Claude Code, so a project-bound skill lands in
`<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope.

DiscoveredSkill.description: One skill a machine really has. `plugin` skills come from an installed plugin.

description.description: The SKILL.md front matter's `description`, when it has one.

path.description: Absolute path of the skill's directory, for the reader and for adoption.

DamagedRow.description:
What the hub lays over a session row whose record, or whose workspace's
record, is damaged on its machine ({@link DamagedRecordReport}): the file,
why, and the way out that removes it (`archive`: archive workspace
`workspaceId`; `end`: end the session).

SessionTooling.description: What a session's `init` says about its MCP servers and tools.

BlockMetadata.description: Everything a renderer may need beyond `content`, keyed by the kind that uses it.

accountMove.description: A `system.account_move`: what the hub did at the session's account's limit.

asked.description: Moved because a person asked (`POST /api/instances/:id/account`), not at a limit.

compact.description:
Moved at its limit to another organization with a context of the
policy's `moveWholeUnderK` or more: it files its open items, then is
compacted natively, as its first steps on `to`. The line is said
again under its id as that goes.

sameOrganization.description: Both accounts in one organization: its prompt cache came along.

window.description: The window that refused it, as {@link windowWords} names it.

resetsAt.description: When that window resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

because.description:
Why it moved other than at a limit: its account was forecast to run
out at `runsOutAt` (a rebalance between turns), its cache was cold at
its wake, so the move re-read nothing extra, or Claude Code refused
`from`'s credential for good (`refused`: the hub signed it out there).
Absent: its account's limit refused a turn, or a person asked.

cost.description: What the re-read cost on `to`: a percent of its window; absent when unpriced.

account.description: The account it is held on, at its limit.

frees.description:
Another account that frees before `account` resets: it moves there
at `until`. Absent: `until` is `account`'s own reset.

until.description: The earliest moment an account takes it again, epoch ms: the line counts down to it.

kind.description:
History only, from before the hub compacted natively: the session
went on in a fresh conversation of its own, seeded with a summary of
the one before, the same session with its account changed (`from`
to `to`; null on a harness without accounts). Lines a hub stored
then still read, between the conversations they divide.

writtenOn.description: The account whose summariser wrote the summary it went on from.

asked.description: The session asked for it (`continue_session`), not its account's limit.

asks.description: It restarted from the person's own messages alone: nothing was summarised.

preparedAtPct.description: The window's percent when the summary was written ahead of the limit; null when it was written at the move.

kind.description:
A work item's session whose project has Caw off: nothing wakes a
model there, so nothing carries it on past `account`'s limit,
neither a move nor a resume at the reset. A person sends it on.

resetsAt.description: When that limit resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

kind.description:
Claude Code refused `account`'s credential for good and no other
account can take the session: it stays, and what it is sent waits at
the hub, until `account` is signed in again or another comes free.

The session's process was ended, and by whom: a stop someone asked
for, or a signal from outside CawCo. A stop is never a failure; the
line says what starts it again.

Moving it whole to `to` failed at `step`: it goes on in its
conversation, still on `from`. (`continue`, a continuation from a
summary, and `asked`, are history only: lines a hub stored before it
compacted natively.)

action.description: What failed: a move whole (`move`), or, in a stored line, a continuation from a summary (`continue`).

signedOut.description: It was moving off `from` because Claude Code refused `from`'s sign-in: `from` has no reset to wait for.

asked.description: The session asked for it (`continue_session`), not its account's limit.

reason.description: What the hub got from the step that failed.

waits.description:
Only work its process holds for later kept it (a background task, a
one-time wake-up): the move goes when that ends, or after
{@link RESTART_WAIT_CAP_MS} at the latest, ending it.

artifactId.description: An artifact responses note's artifact ({@link import ("./harness").ARTIFACT_RESPONSES}): what its line opens.

artifactKind.description: That artifact's kind, which picks its line's glyph.

artifactLead.description: The words its line says before the artifact's name, by the notice it draws (core `ARTIFACT_NOTICES`): "Comments on", "Fix tray handed you".

artifactName.description: That artifact's name, as its line says it.

askRequestId.description: A `user.delegate_ask`'s hub permission requestId — what it waits on to be answered.

attachments.description:
What the reader attached to the turn: texts, parsed back out of its
`<pasted-text>` blocks, and files, out of its `Attached file:` lines.

compactResult.description:
A compaction boundary read back from a harness that stores how it ended
(opencode): `failed` with the harness's words in `compactError`.

continuation.description:
A send that is the message a session went on from in a fresh
conversation (origin {@link import ("./harness").CONTINUATION_ORIGIN}):
drawn folded under the `continued` line before it, never as a turn.

delegateInstanceId.description: The delegate a `tool.handoff` started, read once off its result.

delegateTitle.description: The delegate's brief headline, carried beside {@link delegateInstanceId}.

errorTitle.description:
A failure card's heading (`ui.error`, `ui.session_error`); a missing
session's when unset on a session error, "Turn failed" otherwise.

images.description: A stored transcript can name an image it no longer carries, hence the optional src.

noteKind.description: Harness-injected user-role content (task notifications, reminders, compaction).

noteTaskToolId.description: A task notification's Task `tool_use_id` — folds the note into its branch.

peerName.description: Its display name, as the sender's host asserted it.

peerSession.description: The sender's host-openable session, so the card can link back to it.

permissionMode.description: `init` only, and re-reported every turn: what the session answers tools with.

reportHeadline.description: A delegate report's one-or-two-sentence outcome, from `finish_item`'s `headline`; the body is the full report.

reportKind.description: Set when a `user.peer` is a delegate's auto-report rather than a hand-off.

resultImages.description: Images returned by the tool, as the hub's media references.

ruleName.description: A `user.rule`'s rule name, read off its `[Rule: <name>]` marker line.

sendFailed.description: Why a send did not go: its record's reason.

sendRefusal.description: What refused it, when the hub did: its record's refusal.

skills.description: `init` only: which of the commands are skills rather than commands.

slashCommands.description: `init` only: what this session answers behind `/`, without the leading slash.

subagentModel.description: The `model` override the spawn input asked for, when present.

thinkingDurationMs.description:
How long the thinking block ran, measured by the hub's clock between the
block opening and its settled message. Preferred over transcript
adjacency, which reads 0 when thinking and a tool call land in one frame.

toolDiff.description: The unified file diff returned by an apply_patch call.

tooling.description: `init` only: the MCP servers and tools behind the `/` palette.

toolUseResult.description: The reader's answers to an `AskUserQuestion`, normalised by the harness adapter.

workflowEvent.description: Set when a `user.peer` is a workflow's notice: what happened, e.g. `step Build failed`.

NamedAccount.description: An account as a transcript line names it, as it was when the line was written.

AccountHue.description: The colour an account is drawn in: the `--account-<name>` token.

WaitReason.description:
Why a session at its account's limit waits for the reset rather than
moving: it is a fork (it reads its origin's cache, on its origin's
account), moving is switched off, no other account has room, the reset
comes sooner than re-reading its context elsewhere is worth, or the limit
refused the hub's word to a live work item and the routing has that carry
on after the reset ({@link DelegateWork} `resume`).

EndedBy.description:
Who ended a session's process ({@link AccountMove} `ended`): a person (the
dashboard's Stop), a session (its parent's `stop_delegate`, a lead), the
hub's own work (`why`: a work item over, a workflow step, a project
forgotten), or a signal no part of CawCo sent (`outside`), after which the
turn it cut is handed back when there was one (`resumes`).

ContinueStep.description:
The steps of continuing a session from a summary, in order: read its
transcript, summarise it, start its fresh conversation. Until the last
one is done it goes on in the conversation it has.

landing gate's shared machine slot, a machine's pause, its turn to land):

failed (first lines).

paused until 00:57". Its session runs no turn until then. Null otherwise.

paused until 00:57"), when that is what it waits for; null once it has

waitUntil.description: A declared wait's deadline in epoch ms.

bin.description: The executable whose presence means installed.

dependencyOnly.description:

the policy list until something needs them, and the dashboard shows them
only where they explain another tool's state.

exactVersion.description:
The one version this fleet runs, for a tool CawCo's own code is built
against: every install puts exactly this one on the machine, whatever the
policy pins, and a probe that finds another reports it failed.

install.description: Ordered by preference. Empty for a platform = unsupported there.

requires.description:

automatically (depth 1 — requirements do not have requirements); one that
is present but below `min` does not: silently replacing a machine's Node
is ruder than telling the user exactly what is too old.

versionCommand.description: Probe for the version; the first `x.y.z` in its output is the answer.

wellKnownPaths.description:

probed with `~` expanded, after `which` misses. An installer that edits
shell rc files fixes the *user's* PATH, never a daemon that is already
running.

ToolInstallMethod.description:
One way to put a tool on a machine. Methods are tried in catalog order; the
first whose `platforms` match and whose `needs` is present wins. There is no
fallback past a method that ran and failed — a half-applied installer chain
is harder to reason about than one honest failure.

command.description:
The install command, run through the Bun shell. Exactly one of `command`
and `native` is set.

footprint.description:
How a binary this method put on a machine is told apart, from where it
resolves. A tool already present is installed again only with the method
whose footprint it bears, never a first-eligible one beside it: two
package managers each holding a copy is two copies on the PATH, and the
one that wins is not the one just installed.

label.description: Names the method in status and errors: 'curl script', 'npm', 'winget'.

native.description:
The name of a routine the agent implements in code, for the installs a
portable shell one-liner cannot express (resolving the right Node tarball
for an arch, say). The escape hatch that keeps `command` honest.

needs.description:
A binary that must already be on the machine for this method to be
eligible — 'npm', 'brew', 'winget'. Absent means always eligible.

pinnedCommand.description:

Kept apart from `command` because "latest" is not a version most
installers accept: the curl scripts and winget want no version argument
at all when they should take the newest.

pinnedVersion.description: Exact version to install; null rides `{version}` as `latest`.

required.description: Required tools install automatically wherever a register finds them missing.

scope.description:

- `user` — every machine, every project. MCP goes to `~/.claude.json`'s
  top-level `mcpServers`, skills to `~/.claude/skills/`, plugins install
  `--scope user`. The default, and what most rows want.
- `local` — one project, privately: `~/.claude.json`'s
  `projects["<cwd>"].mcpServers`, the map Claude Code already keeps per
  checkout and git never sees; plugins `--scope local`. What a
  project-bound row should be unless the reader asks to share it.
- `project` — one project, shared with whoever clones it: `.mcp.json` at
  the repo root, plugins `--scope project`. It writes inside the working
  tree, so it is never the default.

`<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope.

once its boundary was closed (schema.ts `workspaces.holding`), and where

Set when the clone's folder is there and its `.git` is no repository
git can read: how many entries down its tree are not CawCo's (agent
stand-ins.ts `straysIn`, which names each by its path relative to the
folder). CawCo's are a deny path's stand-in exactly as made, a mount
point a sandbox left on a deny path, a `.git/config` holding only
git-lfs's `[lfs] repositoryformatversion = 0` marker, a project skill
exactly as CawCo placed it (agent fleet.ts `placedAsMade`), and a
dir (`.git`, `.claude`) holding only those. None is a husk, a deleted
clone a sandbox refilled, which holds nothing; any keeps the folder.

WorkspaceState.description:
A workspace's life, which is its work items' (work-items.ts `settle`):
`active` while an item there is live, or ended a moment ago and the hub
has not settled it, or while something holds it (a session attached, an
artifact showing what it serves); `held` once its item ended with work
that is nowhere else, which only the person ends, by continuing it or
discarding it; `archived` once its boundary and clone are gone.

WorkspaceHolding.description:
What a workspace holds that is nowhere else, read with git on its machine's
host once its boundary is closed (agent workspace.ts `closeClone`): commits
on HEAD or any local branch that no remote-tracking ref has (`git rev-list
--count HEAD --branches --not --remotes`: landed work was pushed, whether
onto the base or to a branch of its own), entries of `git status
--porcelain` (untracked files included; the paths `skip` names, the outputs
its items handed over, left out), and stash entries. Files git ignores are
none of it: they go with the clone, and a delegate keeps one by handing it
in as an output. `bytes` is the clone's size on disk.

git can read: how many entries down its tree are not CawCo's (agent

one that landed as a branch or a pull request), fetched as the clone is.

Who bills the account: a provider id. `anthropic` is a Claude subscription

reset, or move whole to an account known to have room (the hub's

`moveWholeUnderK`: a context under this many thousand tokens moves whole
and goes on; one of this many or more, moved to another organization
(whose cache it can't read), also files its open items and is compacted by
Claude Code's own `/compact` as its first steps there, before anything it
is owed. `delegateWork`: what a turn the limit refused is answered with
when it was the hub's own word to a live work item's session
({@link DelegateWork}); every other word of the hub's a limit refused is
left until a person or the session's parent writes.

`resume`: that word is sent again once, when the account's limit resets;
nothing moves it meanwhile. `move`: it is answered as a person's turn is,
moved whole to an account with room by the routing. `leave`: it waits
until a person or its parent writes to it.
